EnableNpcGenerator.Name: Enable NPC Generator
EnableNpcGenerator.Hint: Adds a tab to NPC sheets that randomly rolls a name, instinct, and trait.

EnableMonsterGenerator.Name: Enable Monster Stat Generator
EnableMonsterGenerator.Hint: Adds a tab to NPC sheets that randomly rolls a damage die, armor, HP, and coin.

EnableAttackAssistant.Name: Enable Attack Damage Automation
EnableAttackAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success, asks whether to roll damage and automatically deducts consumables like ammo. Which moves trigger this is managed in the name lists below and the Special Attack Moves setting.

MeleeMoveNames.Name: Melee Move Names
MeleeMoveNames.Hint: Melee moves like Hack & Slash that always roll damage on success/partial with no choices involved (comma separated). Adjust this if a translation module renamed the move. Moves whose behavior depends on a choice (like Backstab) are managed separately in Special Attack Moves.

RangedMoveNames.Name: Ranged Move Names
RangedMoveNames.Hint: Ranged moves like Volley that always roll damage on success/partial with no choices involved (comma separated). These also trigger the ammo consumption prompt. Moves whose behavior depends on a choice (like Called Shot) are managed separately in Special Attack Moves.

MeleeWeaponTags.Name: Melee Weapon Tags
MeleeWeaponTags.Hint: If a weapon's tags contain any of these keywords (comma separated), it's treated as melee. Weapons have no explicit melee/ranged field; this relies on the Dungeon World convention that melee weapons use hand/close/reach. A weapon matching neither this list nor Ranged Weapon Tags still shows up in the weapon picker (it isn't excluded).

RangedWeaponTags.Name: Ranged Weapon Tags
RangedWeaponTags.Hint: If a weapon's tags contain any of these keywords (comma separated), it's treated as ranged. Dungeon World's convention is that ranged weapons use near/far. Default: near, far.

TagMenu.Name: Damage Tag Automation
TagMenu.Label: Edit Tag List
TagMenu.Hint: Individually toggle which weapon tags are automatically applied when rolling damage.

AttackMovesMenu.Name: Special Attack Moves
AttackMovesMenu.Label: Edit Special Attack Moves
AttackMovesMenu.Hint: Register/edit attack moves whose damage depends on a choice, like Backstab or Called Shot, by name, ranged flag, and behavior. Defaults to the English names (Backstab, Called Shot); edit the name field if your game uses a translated name.

EnableSpellcastingAssistant.Name: Enable Spellcasting Assistant
EnableSpellcastingAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success for a Cast a Spell-type move, asks which prepared spell was used, tracks ongoing spells, and applies a penalty to the next casting.

CastSpellMoveNames.Name: Cast Spell Move Names
CastSpellMoveNames.Hint: The Cleric/Wizard "Cast a Spell" move names (comma separated, translated if applicable). Defaults to the English originals (Cast A Spell, Cast a Spell).

OngoingSpellsMenu.Name: Ongoing Spells
OngoingSpellsMenu.Label: Edit Ongoing Spells
OngoingSpellsMenu.Hint: Register/edit which spells affect future spellcasting rolls while maintained, by name and penalty type. Spells not listed are treated as one-shot.

SpellAugmentationMoveNames.Name: Spell Augmentation Move Names
SpellAugmentationMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that let the caster end an ongoing spell to add its level to damage dealt. Only asked when the actor has this move and an active ongoing spell.

CastPartialRevokeIndex.Name: Cast Spell Partial - Revoke Option Number
CastPartialRevokeIndex.Hint: Which numbered choice in the Cast a Spell partial-success list is "the spell is revoked (unusable until you commune/prepare spells again)"? Position 3 in the default Dungeon World text. Set to 0 to disable this effect.

CastPartialPenaltyIndex.Name: Cast Spell Partial - Penalty Option Number
CastPartialPenaltyIndex.Hint: Which numbered choice in the Cast a Spell partial-success list is "-1 to cast a spell until you commune/prepare spells again"? Position 2 in the default Dungeon World text. Set to 0 to disable this effect.

TranslationImportMenu.Name: Auto-fill from Translation Module
TranslationImportMenu.Label: Open Auto-fill Tool
TranslationImportMenu.Hint: If the Nomal-1/dungeonworld-ko Korean translation module is installed, fill in the move/spell name settings above using its translation data instead of typing them by hand.

EnableHitTriggerAssistant.Name: Enable Hit-Taken Automation
EnableHitTriggerAssistant.Hint: When a player character's HP is about to drop, asks whether to negate the damage using a move like Armor Mastery or Bloody Aegis (at the cost of armor or a debility) before the HP change is applied. Which moves qualify is managed in the Hit-Taken Moves setting below.

HitTriggerMovesMenu.Name: Hit-Taken Moves
HitTriggerMovesMenu.Label: Edit Hit-Taken Moves
HitTriggerMovesMenu.Hint: Register/edit moves that can negate incoming damage at a cost, by name and effect (lower armor by 1, or take a debility of your choice). "Grants +1 forward" is for moves like Armored Perfection that also grant a bonus on top of negating the damage.

IndomitableMoveNames.Name: Indomitable Move Names
IndomitableMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that grant +1 forward whenever the character takes a new debility, for any reason (including from Bloody Aegis).

EnableHealingAssistant.Name: Enable Healing Automation
EnableHealingAssistant.Hint: On a success or partial success for a healing move (Lay On Hands), or when a healing spell (Cure Light/Moderate/Critical Wounds, Heal) is cast via the Cast a Spell flow, asks who to heal and rolls (or asks for) the amount, then applies it. The recipient can be anyone the healer at least has observer access to (handy for narratively-ambiguous allies/enemies); if the healer doesn't have full access, an online GM is asked to approve before it's applied. Which moves/spells qualify is managed in the Healing Moves setting below.

HealingMovesMenu.Name: Healing Moves
HealingMovesMenu.Label: Edit Healing Moves
HealingMovesMenu.Hint: Register/edit moves and spells that heal, by name and how to determine the amount: automatically (reads the spell's own roll formula, or an inline dice notation like [[1d8]] in the move's own text), a custom formula you type in, or "up to max HP" (prompts for a number, for Heal). Check "Transfer to self on partial" for moves like Lay On Hands whose partial-success result transfers the healing (or disease) to the healer instead.

HospitallerMovesMenu.Name: Hospitaller Moves
HospitallerMovesMenu.Label: Edit Hospitaller Moves
HospitallerMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Hospitaller/Perfect Hospitaller that add extra healing whenever the character heals someone else (not themselves), by name and bonus dice formula.

EnableMoveUpgradeAssistant.Name: Enable Move Upgrade Automation
EnableMoveUpgradeAssistant.Hint: When a character learns an advanced move that upgrades an earlier one (e.g. Perfect Hospitaller upgrading Hospitaller), automatically removes the earlier move from the sheet. Which pairs count is managed in the Move Upgrades setting below.

MoveUpgradesMenu.Name: Move Upgrades
MoveUpgradesMenu.Label: Edit Move Upgrades
MoveUpgradesMenu.Hint: Register pairs of moves where learning the first one automatically removes the second. Pre-filled with all 43 such pairs found across the 8 core classes' compendium data (each advanced move's own "requires" field).

DamageReductionMovesMenu.Name: Damage Reduction Moves
DamageReductionMovesMenu.Label: Edit Damage Reduction Moves
DamageReductionMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Underdog/Serious Underdog that reduce incoming damage by a flat amount under some fictional condition (e.g. being outnumbered) that can't be auto-detected — asked as Y/N right before the damage lands, by name and amount.

ConditionalDamageMovesMenu.Name: Conditional Damage Moves
ConditionalDamageMovesMenu.Label: Edit Conditional Damage Moves
ConditionalDamageMovesMenu.Hint: Register moves like Smite/Holy Smite/Exterminatus or Viper's Strike/Fangs that add a dice bonus (or penalty) to a damage roll depending on a fictional condition that can't be auto-detected (being on a Quest, dual-wielding, etc.) — asked as Y/N when rolling damage. "Yes"/"No" formula are added to the roll; leave a formula blank or "0" to add nothing for that answer. Check "Requires Designation" for moves like Exterminatus whose effect doesn't exist at all until a target is declared (adds a designated/not-designated toggle on the sheet; while not designated, the move is completely ignored).

SuperiorWarriorMoveNames.Name: Superior Warrior Move Names
SuperiorWarriorMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that announce in chat whenever a melee attack move reaches an extreme success (12+).

EnableDruidAssistant.Name: Enable Druid Assistant
EnableDruidAssistant.Hint: Adds a character sheet tab for Druids showing a Balance counter (gained whenever the character deals damage via the automated attack flow, spendable to heal someone) and Shapeshift state (active/inactive, current animal form, and a free-text note area for the GM).

DruidBalanceMoveNames.Name: Druid Balance Move Names
DruidBalanceMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) whose owner gains 1 Balance whenever they deal damage through this module's attack automation.

DruidShapeshifterMoveNames.Name: Druid Shapeshifter Move Names
DruidShapeshifterMoveNames.Hint: Move names (comma separated) that, on a success or partial success, ask for the new animal form's name and mark the character as shapeshifted. Also auto-sets Hold from the move's own result text (e.g. "Hold 3").

Forceful.Note: Forceful: you can knock them back or off their feet

Messy.Note: Messy: forces a losing side into a hard choice

TagSettings.Title: Damage Tag Automation
TagSettings.Hint: If a checked tag is present on the weapon, its raw text is shown in the damage roll message. Tags marked "auto-applied by the damage buttons" (damage bonus / piercing / ignores armor) are picked up by Dungeon World's own full/half/double/heal damage-apply buttons when clicked — the system reads the message text itself; this module doesn't calculate anything. Those buttons apply to whichever tokens are selected on the canvas (not targeted), and require the Dungeon World system setting "Enable Damage Buttons" to be on (default: on). Tags marked "shown as a note only" (Forceful/Messy) have no system automation, so they're just displayed for the GM to judge.

AttackMoves.Title: Special Attack Moves
AttackMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). Check "Ranged" to also trigger the ammo consumption prompt. Check "Choice gates damage" to only roll damage when the player picks a choice containing a damage die (e.g. 1d6) — this is Backstab's behavior. Leave it unchecked if the choices are just flavor and damage is decided purely by the partial/success checkboxes — this is Called Shot's behavior. The partial/success pick counts try to auto-detect the move's own "Choose N" text, but that text disappears under translation, so specifying the number here directly is more reliable.
AttackMoves.Name: Move Name

OngoingSpells.Hint: Register spells that affect future spellcasting rolls while maintained. Enter the name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable).

TranslationImport.Title: Auto-fill from Translation Module
TranslationImport.Hint: Reads the move/spell name pairs bundled with the Nomal-1/dungeonworld-ko Korean translation module and uses them to fill in this module's move/spell name settings (melee/ranged move names, Cast a Spell move names, Spell Augmentation move names, Special Attack Moves, Ongoing Spells, Hit-Taken Moves, Indomitable Move Names, Healing Moves, Hospitaller Moves, Move Upgrades, Damage Reduction Moves, Conditional Damage Moves, Superior Warrior Move Names, Druid Balance Move Names, Druid Shapeshifter Move Names). Names not found in the translation data (third-party moves, names you already edited by hand) are left untouched.

HitTriggerMoves.Title: Hit-Taken Moves
HitTriggerMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). "Effect" decides what the player gives up to negate the damage: lower armor by 1, or take a debility of their choice (if all 6 debilities are already taken, the move can't be used and won't be offered). Check "Grants +1 forward" for moves like Armored Perfection that also grant a bonus (Dungeon World's own forward attribute, auto-applied to the next roll and then cleared).
HitTriggerMoves.Name: Move Name

HitTrigger.PromptContent: {name} is about to take {damage} damage. Negate it using one of these moves?
HitTrigger.DebilityInstruction: Choose a debility to take instead.
HitTrigger.ArmorDestroyed: {name}'s armor has reached 0 — remember to remove/destroy the depleted armor or shield on the sheet.
HitTrigger.ReductionPrompt: Are you currently outnumbered ("{name}")? If so, this damage is reduced.

DamageReductionMoves.Title: Damage Reduction Moves
DamageReductionMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). Right before damage lands, the player is asked Y/N whether the fictional condition applies; if yes, incoming damage is reduced by "Amount" (floored at 0).
DamageReductionMoves.Name: Move Name

ConditionalDamageMoves.Title: Conditional Damage Moves
ConditionalDamageMoves.Hint: Enter the move name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). When rolling damage, the player is asked Y/N whether the fictional condition applies, then the matching formula is added to the damage roll. Use a plain dice/number expression (e.g. "1d4", "2d4", "-4"); leave blank or "0" to add nothing for that answer.
ConditionalDamageMoves.Name: Move Name

ConditionalDamage.Prompt: Does the condition for "{name}" apply to this attack?
ConditionalDamage.ReverseNo: Reverse penalty triggered: {formula} (this attack wasn't against the designated target)
ConditionalDamage.AutoNoTitle: Click to toggle whether this move's "No" answer is applied automatically without asking every time (handy while the condition clearly won't be met for a while, e.g. your marked enemy fled)
ConditionalDamage.DesignationTitle: Click to toggle whether a target has been designated. While not designated, this move does nothing at all (no prompt, no bonus, no penalty).

SuperiorWarrior.Applied: Extreme success (12+): deal damage, avoid the enemy's attack, and impress/dismay/frighten it.

HealingMoves.Title: Healing Moves
HealingMoves.Hint: Enter the move/spell name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable). "Automatic" reads the spell's own roll formula, or an inline dice notation in the move's own success/partial text; fall back to "Custom formula" if that fails (e.g. under translation) or the move doesn't have one. "Up to max HP" prompts for a number instead of rolling (for Heal). Check "Transfer to self on partial" only for moves whose own partial result explicitly transfers the healing/harm to the healer (Lay On Hands).
HealingMoves.Name: Move/Spell Name

HospitallerMoves.Title: Hospitaller Moves
HospitallerMoves.Hint: Register moves that add extra healing whenever the character heals someone else (not themselves). Enter the name exactly as it appears in your game (translated, if applicable).
HospitallerMoves.Name: Move Name

MoveUpgrades.Title: Move Upgrades
MoveUpgrades.Hint: Enter both names exactly as they appear in your game (translated, if applicable). When a character gains a move item matching "Upgrade Move", any move on the same actor matching "Replaced Move" is deleted automatically.
